title: Plato–Aristotle authorship: measures, controls and pre-registered predictions
description: The Measurement Register (#1570), pre-registrations (#1571) and notebook (#1569), August 2026, set out what the Plato–Aristotle investigation measured and predicted. Its theses argue that Aristotle completes executions Plato abandoned, that his charges against Plato name properties of his own corpus, and that he compiled the record (#1582). Tests require labelled controls (the Attic orators, Albert→Aquinas, Sappho→Catullus) before the target is scored. Later entries revise earlier ones: #1571 replaces its yield measure; the notebook gives the charges class as proposed where the register gave it as measured, reverses its survival question and reformulates a reading #1576 narrows; #1671 (October) corrects the premise of Theophrastus's inheritance by will. The notebook claims Plato is Aristotle's heteronym; #1571 holds one historical hand live, not established.
